last.verdict: Chemicals growth and far lower interest costs lifted profit, but Print is shrinking and its profit has nearly vanished.

takeaways.label: Chemicals carry the company
takeaways.text: Advanced Materials & Chemicals revenue rose 21% to $99 million, with operating profit (EBITDA) up to $21 million from $16 million. Growth slowed from last quarter's 40%.

takeaways.label: Print profit nearly gone
takeaways.text: Print revenue fell 7% to $165 million on lower prepress and press volumes. Its operating profit (EBITDA) dropped to $1 million from $8 million a year ago.

takeaways.label: Net income helped by debt paydown
takeaways.text: Net income rose to $21 million from $13 million, mostly because interest expense fell to $3 million from $18 million. Operating profit (EBITDA) rose only $2 million, to $31 million.

takeaways.label: Cash up, costs rising
takeaways.text: Cash rose $27 million to $317 million, but year-to-date operating cash flow is only break-even. Overhead rose to $50 million from $41 million, driven by stock pay and benefit accruals.

history.verdict: Kodak's fourth straight year-over-year improvement, with gross profit up 61% and net income of $17 million, now has less debt behind it.

takeaways.label: Margins jumped
takeaways.text: Gross margin rose to 26% from 19% as higher prices and volume outran pricier silver and aluminum. Operational EBITDA reached $36 million, up from $9 million.

takeaways.label: Chemicals led growth
takeaways.text: Advanced Materials & Chemicals revenue rose 40% to $105 million and its operational EBITDA nearly tripled to $22 million. Print grew 10% and swung to an $8 million profit.

takeaways.label: Debt sharply reduced
takeaways.text: Kodak repaid $101 million of term loans and cut interest expense by $9 million. Management said total debt to EBITDA is 1x, versus 23x a year earlier.

takeaways.label: Cash and pension caveats
takeaways.text: Cash fell $47 million to $290 million as inventory rose $37 million on silver and aluminum. Pension income is expected to stay below last year's level through 2026.
